title: Huang sensitivity / interlacing on the ES certificate hypercube
connection: Huang's proof uses a signed adjacency matrix of the hypercube and Cauchy interlacing to force a high-degree vertex in any large induced subgraph; ES certificates live on a product of small 'choice' cubes (choice of prime factors into a,b).
why: Interlacing arguments convert 'large set' into 'has a forced structure' — the repo noted Hoffman/Huang bounds depending only on |A| fail; a signed-matrix variant with the χ structure is still open.
first_step: Construct a signing of the divisor-lattice cube of N such that the eigenvalue bound encodes the class −1 mod e; test numerically on hard primes.
alt_first_steps: [upgrades-0124] Model: vertices = subsets S, label g(S) = Π_{i∈S} q_i mod e; find the maximal size of a set of subsets with no two labels in ratio −1, compare with 2^{k−1}.
[upgrades-0293] Compute by brute force, for e ≤ 50 and k ≤ 12 with random labels, the maximum certificate-free subset family size.
refs: Huang, Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture, Ann. Math. 190 (2019), arXiv:1907.00847
arXiv:1907.00847 (Huang, Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture)
repo_note: Huang sensitivity dismissed as cosmetic analogy; signed divisor-cube construction not tested.

title: Is ES critical or supercritical? Fractional expectation threshold of the level hypergraph
connection: Park–Pham relate thresholds to expectation thresholds. The repo measures ≈ (0.44 → 0.97)·log p expected hit levels (critical regime). Compute, in a random model matching ES's level statistics, the threshold for 'some level hits' and see whether ES sits above it by a growing margin.
why: If ES is only 'critically' above threshold in natural models, any proof must exploit non-random structure; if supercritical, second-moment-type methods are favoured.
first_step: Simulate the matched random model and compute P(no hit) as a function of the scaling parameter; compare with data for hard primes.
alt_first_steps: [tools-0072] Model prime factors of 4Cp+1 (C ≤ X) as independent with Mertens probabilities, compute expectation threshold vs actual threshold numerically.
[upgrades-0142] Compute the fractional expectation threshold of the (★) certificate family for test p using LP over levels.
refs: arXiv:2203.17207 (Park-Pham, A proof of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture)
Park–Pham, A proof of the Kahn–Kalai conjecture, arXiv:2203.17207
repo_note: Park–Pham thresholds judged inapplicable at fixed p; matched random-model threshold not simulated.

title: Decoupling/energy for the hyperbolic ES surface {4uBC − u − B}
connection: BDG decoupling bounds moments of exponential sums over curves. Additive energy of the ES-word set (#{w₁ = w₂} with w = 4uBC−u−B ≤ N) controls the second moment Σ_n R(n)².
why: Second-moment control is the ingredient of every almost-all → pointwise attempt via variance; decoupling-type bounds for this specific surface could be sharp.
first_step: Compute the energy E(N) = Σ_{n≤N} R(n)² for N up to 10⁷ and fit N·(log N)^a; compare with what a decoupling inequality for (u, B, uB) would predict.
alt_first_steps: [tools-0105] Write Σ_n f(n) e(nα) as an exponential sum over the surface and identify a moment-curve-like structure for decoupling.
refs: arXiv:1512.01565 (Bourgain-Demeter-Guth)

title: U_n as a Looijenga pair: Gross–Hacking–Keel theta functions on the ES log CY surface
connection: The projective closure 4xyz = nw(xy+yz+zx) minus the triangle w = 0 is a log Calabi–Yau surface with a toric model: P² blown up at three collinear boundary points (GEOMETRY_ES Prop 2.1). GHK construct a canonical basis of theta functions on the mirror family of any Looijenga pair, indexed by integral points of the tropicalisation.
why: Theta functions give canonical regular functions with positive structure constants. If positive integer points of U_n correspond to positivity of some theta function's values, the native existence tools are scattering diagrams.
first_step: Read GHKS 'The mirror of the cubic surface' and check whether the nodal (Cayley) degeneration with boundary through nodes is covered; compute the tropicalisation of U_n.
alt_first_steps: [translate-0043] Compute the scattering diagram of the Looijenga pair (Y_n, D) (three collinear blow-up points). Check whether ES's special position (collinearity) makes it finite (cluster-type) or infinite.
refs: arXiv:1106.4977 (Gross–Hacking–Keel, Mirror symmetry for log Calabi–Yau surfaces I)

title: Li–Zhang's theorem on Kudla–Rapoport: unitary special cycles and an arithmetic Diff-parity
connection: KUDLA_ES links T1 to oddness of Kudla's Diff(T). In the unitary setting, Li–Zhang proved the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture (arithmetic intersection numbers = derivatives of local densities).
why: If ES certificates are special cycles on a unitary Shimura variety, intersection numbers have exact local formulas, and positivity is geometric.

title: Rademacher symbol (conjugacy-invariant) = linking number of the modular knot with the trefoil (Ghys)
connection: Ghys: for hyperbolic γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ), the Rademacher symbol (the conjugacy-invariant version of Rademacher's function Φ, differing by a sign/trace correction) equals the linking number of the closed geodesic (modular knot) in SL₂(ℝ)/SL₂(ℤ) = S³ − trefoil with the trefoil. If the ES sign is a function of Φ(γ_w), it becomes a linking number.
why: A topological meaning for the sign would bring knot-theoretic positivity/counting (Ghys's theorem) to ES; at least it is an exact dictionary.
first_step: Compute Φ(γ_w) for words (from the cutting sequence) and test whether Φ mod 4 determines the slot-lemma sign.
alt_first_steps: [tools-0165] Compute Rademacher symbols Ψ(M) for ES₅ certificate matrices at many p and look for a forced value range.
refs: Ghys, Knots and dynamics (ICM 2006)

title: Supersingular isogeny graphs: certificates as short cycles / collisions in the ℓ-isogeny graph mod p
connection: Maximal orders in B_{p,∞} ↔ supersingular curves over F̄_p. Embeddings of CM orders ↔ endomorphisms. ES Type I ⇔ a CM-order collision, which might be a short closed walk in an isogeny graph (Pizer graphs, Ramanujan).
why: Ramanujan-graph expansion gives existence of short walks between any vertices, which is a pointwise existence mechanism (T-type thick object of size ~p/12).
first_step: For p < 500, compute which supersingular j-invariants have endomorphism rings containing the orders Λ_{d,m} and how ES levels map to isogeny degrees.

title: Geodesic-flow coding (Series) of γ_w: ES₅ as a closed geodesic with 3 cusp excursions of prescribed depths
connection: Caroline Series' coding links the cutting sequence of a geodesic to its CF expansion, so cusp-excursion depths correspond to partial quotients. A word gives a closed geodesic whose (HJ) coding has 3 blocks of depths (v, t, u), plus a p-condition.
why: Shrinking-target and logarithm-law results (Sullivan) describe cusp excursions statistically. Prescribed exact-depth triples relate to 'periodic orbits with prescribed excursions' counts (Pollicott, Lalley).
first_step: Count closed geodesics whose coding is exactly a 3-block HJ word with depths in given ranges; compare with the word count via the p-constraint.
alt_first_steps: [tools-0178] Draw, for hard primes, the Farey path of the relevant rationals and record the minimal crossing count; compare with the length-3 requirement.
refs: Series, The modular surface and continued fractions (J. LMS 1985)

title: Fake-ES models: same local statistics, almost-all holds, infinitely many failures
connection: Kahane–Katznelson show a.e. results can be sharp for any null set. Build synthetic 'ES-like' problems (random divisor data with ES's congruence statistics, or ES with a perturbed rule) where Vaughan's proof goes through verbatim but failures are infinite; the real proof must use a feature the fakes lack.
why: Identifies which properties of the integers any ES proof must use — the constructive face of the barrier map.
first_step: Construct a random model of 'divisors of 4Cp+1' with independent prime-factor classes, run the almost-all argument, and check what pointwise statement fails.
alt_first_steps: [tools-0219] Build a model: random integers with correct local divisibility but with an added sparse 'conspiracy' making all certificates fail for p in a thin set; check consistency with ET averages and Vaughan.

connection: Smooth numbers drove progress on G(k). ES: restrict certificates to smooth (u,B) or smooth 4C, where distribution in progressions to large moduli is better (friable Bombieri–Vinogradov beyond 1/2).

title: Elsholtz-style generalised windmills for x² + ny² as templates for ES windmills
connection: Zagier's one-sentence proof generalises (Elsholtz; Jackson et al.) to involution proofs that primes in certain classes are represented by x² + 2y², x² + 3y², etc. These are verified parity proofs for 'one representation exists' at primes in classes.
why: These are the closest proved windmill-type pointwise theorems. Their combinatorial skeleton (sets of triples with linear involutions) is the template that WINDMILL/INVOLUTION_ES look for, so the known catalogue tells what forms are reachable.
first_step: Collect the known windmill proofs (x² + ny², n ∈ {1,2,3,…}) and their set definitions; check whether the ES Type II data (4abd = pe + 1) can be fitted to any of their shapes.
alt_first_steps: [tools-0285] Search computationally for involutions on finite ES-related sets (e.g. bounded certificate tuples) whose fixed-point count is odd exactly when p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and not a square.

title: Closed horocycle at height 1/p: equidistribution of (a + i)/p and cusp excursions
connection: Every closed horocycle of length → ∞ equidistributes (Sarnak/Hejhal; sparse versions by Venkatesh, Strömbergsson). Points (a + i)/p, a mod p, lift ES₅-type continued-fraction data of a/p; ES₅ needs a point whose cusp excursion has a specific deep shape.

title: Siegel–Weil formula for the certificate genus: average over the genus is the BM main term
connection: Siegel–Weil: the genus-averaged representation number is a product of local densities, i.e. an Eisenstein coefficient. BM's main term is exactly such a product. The difference from a single class is a cusp-form coefficient.
why: In the quadratic-form toolbox, pointwise lower bounds come from 'Eisenstein main term ≫ cusp error'. ES's analogue has main term log²p, too small for cusp bounds; this is the native statement of the B3 obstacle.
first_step: Compute the ratio of BM main term to the trivial cusp-form bound in the best available quadratic encoding (rank 4, QUATERNION_ES); record the exponent gap.
alt_first_steps: [upgrades-0181] Express M_BM as Π of local densities (singular series) for the (★) variety and compare with the BL Brauer-corrected Siegel–Weil heuristics; look for the 'classes' whose average it is.

title: Restricted-denominator ES: which congruence restrictions on x, y, z keep ES true?
connection: Breusch/Stewart: every rational with odd denominator is a sum of distinct odd unit fractions (many terms). For three terms, all-odd is impossible (parity: 4xyz = p(xy+yz+zx) forces an even denominator). Classify restrictions (x,y,z in prescribed classes mod m) that are consistent with ES for all small p, and test which ones look 'every p'.
why: Restricted versions that hold numerically are stronger statements that may carry more structure for a proof (or reveal new obstructions).
first_step: Read arXiv:1108.6118 and arXiv:1606.02117; tabulate which three-term restricted variants of 4/n are known false and true.

title: Positivstellensatz / SOS degree of infeasibility certificates for bounded ES failures
connection: For bounded parameters, 'no certificate at p up to height B' is a finite infeasibility statement with a Positivstellensatz/SOS (or Nullstellensatz) refutation. The degree needed as a function of p and B is a proof-complexity measure.
why: If refutation degree must grow, low-degree 'algebraic' proofs of existence are impossible in a quantifiable sense (analogue of B1). If it stays bounded for some encoding, that encoding has hidden structure.
first_step: For p failing ES₅ at small B (e.g. p = 5, 13, 17, 2521 for I3_𝒞), compute minimal Nullstellensatz degree over F₂ of the bounded infeasibility system.
alt_first_steps: [upgrades-0174] Encode 'no (★) certificate with u, B, C ≤ X' for a fixed true p as an infeasible polynomial system and compute Nullstellensatz degree for small X.
refs: arXiv:1603.04246 (Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 8)
repo_evidence: SOS certificates prove *real* infeasibility or real positivity; ES failures at odd squares are not real-infeasible

title: Class-number formula positivity for the BM correction T(p)
connection: Dirichlet's real-character case: L(1,χ) = (const)·h > 0 because h is a positive integer. M_BM = M₀ − T(p) with T(p) = Σ (−uB/p)/φ(4uB); express T(p) through L(1, (·/p)·ψ) for small auxiliary ψ, i.e. through class numbers of Q(√±p m).
why: If T(p) ≈ c·L(1,(·/p))·(log p) + …, then integrality/positivity of class numbers and known upper bounds of L(1,χ) give an exact grip on the main term, beyond Burgess.
first_step: Inspect BM_CORRECTED_COUNT / BOARD2_SLATE main-term formulas for p-dependent L-value factors; if present, apply Siegel/Burgess lower bounds.
